rules.name: Version control decides the code
rules.statement: A map covers the files a project's version control accounts for, including new files it does not already skip.
rules.risk: Reading everything on disk instead would pull generated output into the map and describe code nobody wrote.

sites.why: Asks version control for the files it already tracks.
Adds files the author created but never registered, minus what version control skips.
The file list for a project starts from version control, not from the folder tree.

rules.name: Build output is not the product
rules.statement: Packaged output, copied-in libraries and lock files never count as a project's own code.
rules.risk: The map would swell with files nobody wrote, burying the code the team actually maintains.

sites.why: Drops every file sitting under a known build, package or vendor folder.
Drops the lock files a package manager writes for itself.
Keeps the same folders out when the project has no version control at all.

rules.name: A project may leave out its own code
rules.statement: A project can list committed code that its map must leave out.
rules.risk: A fixture tree or a copied-in library would count as product code and warp every size and gap number.

sites.why: Keeps the last pattern that matched, so a later line can put a file back.
Answers whether a file is left out, from the pattern that decided it.
Removes the file from the set a build will read.

rules.name: Leaving code out is never silent
rules.statement: Every run reports what a project's own skip list removed, one pattern at a time.
rules.risk: A map could read as complete because the proof of a gap was removed before anyone looked.

sites.why: Says the tree was narrowed on every check, not only the thorough one.
Prints one line per pattern in the briefing a person reads before a build.
Builds the line saying how many files each pattern removed.
Names the patterns that removed nothing, which read as coverage the author never got.

rules.name: One box is a folder-sized unit
rules.statement: One box covers about one folder of code, at most ten files or three thousand lines.
rules.risk: Drawn too big, a box hides whole modules the reader needed to see.

sites.why: A folder inside both limits becomes one box and is not opened further.
One oversized folder holding no subfolders splits into several boxes.
States the size one box should cover, in the instructions a build follows.

rules.name: Coarseness advises, never blocks
rules.statement: Findings about how coarsely a map is drawn are advice, because deliberate abstraction is allowed.
rules.risk: A build would be stopped over a fold its author chose on purpose and can defend.

sites.why: Files a folded-away module as advice rather than as a failure.
Files the box-count nudge as advice rather than as a failure.
The run fails on real errors only, so advice never stops it.

rules.name: A recorded coarse decision stops the advice
rules.statement: A map can record a deliberate coarse decision, and the advice about that decision then stops.
rules.risk: Without the record, a defended decision nags at every check and trains the reader to wave advice through.

sites.why: Reads the folders a map records as deliberately drawn coarsely.
Skips a folder that sits at or under one the map recorded.
Skips the box-count nudge when the map records that altitude decision.

rules.name: A previous map is never an input
rules.statement: The map a build replaces is never an input to the new one.
rules.risk: A rebuild could copy the old wording, so nobody can tell whether the new map is right.

sites.why: Tells a build not to open the map it is replacing.
Warns before a build when a stray map sits among the files to be read.
Keeps the folder holding a map out of the files a build reads.
